title: Evolution searches the space of behaviour-shaping signals rather than local rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution searches the space of behaviour-shaping signals rather than local rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because metazoan cells are agential (they retain adaptive behaviours from unicellular ancestors), what evolution mainly searches is not the enormous space of all possible local rules but the space of behaviour-shaping signals by which cells hack each other's functionality, and the collective intelligence of cell swarms strongly affects the rate and course of evolution.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › From genotype to phenotype in development: implications of an indirect pathway

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I argue that what evolution is really searching is not the enormous space of all possible local rules, but instead the space of behavior-shaping signals by which cells hack each other’s functionality, and that the collective intelligence [38, 39] of cellular swarms has major implications for the rate and course of evolution.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “From genotype to phenotype in development: implications of an indirect pathway”. Scope: Evolution of metazoan anatomy

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed search advantage has measurable versions in simulations and selected perturbation datasets. Existing data cannot resolve the assertion about what evolution 'really' searches or its major effects across metazoan evolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In explicit evolutionary models, compare adaptation rate and accessible phenotypes when mutation changes local cell rules versus intercellular behaviour-shaping signals, holding parameter counts and mutation budgets constant. Comparative biological evidence could then test whether evolved anatomical changes disproportionately map to signalling changes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Model advantages may reflect representation choices rather than biology.

The two search spaces are difficult to define comparably.

Evolution changes both local rules and signals.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.38
operationalizability: 0.5
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The cited competency model is public, includes saved runs, and can show whether selection shifts onto competency parameters. That is a proxy for one sentence of a much broader claim about what evolution searches in metazoans. Sequence collections do not discriminate behaviour-shaping signals from the rest of the genome as the object of search.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the public artificial-embryogeny model, compare the rate of fitness gain and the fraction of accepted changes in competency rules versus structural genes. Faster search and a shift toward competency edits would support a proxy in which evolution spends its effort on behaviour-shaping rules; equal or greater progress through structural edits would count against that proxy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Elevated evolution of signalling genes is compatible with ordinary selection on phenotypes and does not identify the search space.

The simulation searches a toy axial map, not the space of metazoan cell-behaviour rules.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.65
